Daily Digest · Computer Science

LLMs Show Surprising Blindspots in AI-Assisted Review

Today's papers reveal a troubling pattern: large language models used to review academic papers systematically focus on appendices rather than main content, suggesting fundamental misalignments in how AI assists human evaluation. Alongside this discovery, the research community continues advancing multimodal reasoning, safe agent design, and efficient inference—indicating a field simultaneously grappling with AI's collaborative limitations while pushing toward more capable autonomous systems.

⚡ Highlighted Findings 4 selected · AI-curated
NLP
LLM Reviewers Fixate on Appendices Over Core Claims

GPT and Claude models draw 50%+ of review criticisms from paper appendices rather than main content, suggesting they lack understanding of academic paper structure and importance weighting. This bias directly influences human reviewers who rely on LLM assistance, potentially distorting peer review outcomes.

Latest LLM review models systematically overweight appendix content, raising concerns about AI-assisted academic evaluation.
Ghosh, Saim, Jiang 2611.17811 PDF
AI Safety
Formally Verified Planning Reconciles Safety with Agent Utility

Soteria uses hierarchical planning and runtime enforcement to let LLM agents complete tasks safely without getting trapped in unrecoverable states. Previous approaches sacrificed either safety or utility; this framework achieves both through formal verification before execution.

Verified planning enables agents to satisfy safety constraints while maintaining task completion—solving the safety-utility tension.
He, Desai, Malik, Gupta 2611.17880 PDF
Computer Vision
Vision-as-Tool Decouples Agent Perception from Reasoning

Rather than baking vision into agent architecture, this framework treats visual reasoning as a callable tool, removing the bottleneck where agent performance was bounded by internal perceptual limits. Text-only agents can now perform visual tasks without native perception.

Decoupling vision from agent architecture enables stronger visual reasoning and text-only agents to handle multimodal tasks.
Yang, Wu, Jiang, Cheng, Xia 2611.17797 PDF
Machine Learning
Orthogonal Projection Enables Safe, Efficient LLM Unlearning

UUE reformulates unlearning as a control problem using orthogonal null-space projection to disentangle which knowledge to forget from which to retain. This theoretically grounded approach avoids the utility degradation that plagues fine-tuning-based methods.

Orthogonal projection framework achieves knowledge removal while preserving general model utility with minimal computational cost.
Wang, Liu, Yang, Wang, Jin 2611.17864 PDF
